experiments.name: prefix

intervention.intervention: Preserve unique directory prefixes; construct only first shared/missing suffix before one non-fallible splice.
intervention.workload: Unchanged native fresh scalar/deep and installation 1/8/64/128/256; BPI2 and BPC1 original baseline plus current before and candidate. 3 warmups/9 samples; 3 rotated processes, two windows; allocations separately.
intervention.target: Provisional >=10% install64 median reduction in both windows, lower allocated bytes/calls, no peak increase, no repeated guard regression outside observed control range.
intervention.preservation: Same bytes, results, required effects/cancellation, retained versions, initialized slots, references and fault atomicity. Maximum recursion bounded by machine-word radix depth. Public handles, wire and ownership unchanged.
proof: allocation-failure sweeps over shared root and unique-prefix/shared-suffix paths
zero directory copies on unshared sparse insertion

experiments.disposition: Under 10% target: about 3-5% lower install64 medians; lower allocation work. Retained only within the later combined construction.

experiments.name: inline

intervention.parent: original published pair; excludes prefix-splice candidate
intervention.nomination: candidate / UNI-ORDINARY: inline one Binding or existing radix tree; same handle API
intervention.evidence: 1165 allocations at install64 and allocator 466 sampled leaves; prefix-only candidate misses 10% target
intervention.mechanism: First binding requires no page/directory; fork copies one descriptor; promotion prepares tree before publication; branch/page representation unchanged
intervention.law: View maps slot to initialized value; forks isolate binding versions while retaining graph reference identity. Root storage absent from checkpoints; failure retains logical contents/revision
intervention.falsifier: Retained view changes, promotion failure changes contents/revision, stale iterator accepts, mixed-model mismatch, full-path latency or memory guard fails
intervention.target: >=10% lower install64 median in two rotating windows; lower allocation calls/bytes; no higher peak; no repeatable latency regression outside baseline process ranges
intervention.tradeoff: Larger View table entry and at most one existing-descriptor copy per promotion; inline fork copies one descriptor instead of retaining a page
intervention.proof: mixed flat model, owned-reference identity, failure injection at promotion and subsequent tree mutation, full World aggregate
intervention.invalidators: new storage alternative, handle invalidation, ownership transfer, checkpoint observer, changed workload/build

experiments.disposition: Not selected: misses latency target, increases several working peaks, and adds a root representation.

experiments.name: transfer

intervention.parent: published pair; no prefix or inline changes
intervention.nomination: candidate / UNI-ORDINARY: collect genuine operands, then move Frames entry
intervention.evidence: step removes active frame after control changes; capture forks, prunes shared storage, then discards original. Profile attributes 190 samples to capture pruning.
intervention.law: Same slot bindings and pending/cleanup custody at public boundaries. Gather operands before transfer. Keep multi-shot cloning and resident rollback.
intervention.resources: Constant frame transfer; temporary storage only for real call/effect operands, never full live environments; same arena
intervention.target: >=10% install64 reduction in both windows; lower allocations; no increased peak or repeated guard regression
intervention.invalidators: new capture caller or reader after transfer; observable callback in private transition; required retained original frame

experiments.disposition: Under latency target, but eliminates unnecessary active-frame forks. Refined to preserve node identity.

experiments.name: reuse

intervention.change: Reuse the singly-custodied active control node as its continuation; retain the same frame entry until continuation consumption. Step releases only departed control records.
intervention.authority: state_admission.custodian rejects more than one custodian; all frames require exactly one. No authored value references a control node.
intervention.target: same >=10% install64 latency reduction, lower allocations, no peak increase and unchanged guard semantics
proof: same frame handle and node ID across handle boundary
resident rollback under Store journal plus Frames backup
intervention.fallback: restore original source only; no public format or API change

experiments.disposition: Meets install64 latency target; install8 working peak rises 500 bytes. Resource guard not met.

experiments.name: combined

intervention.change: Add previously isolated unique-prefix splice to active-frame/node transfer; no inline representation
intervention.rationale: Reuse meets install64 latency target but install8 peak grows by 500 bytes. Prefix splice removes unnecessary directory allocations on unique paths.
intervention.target: Unchanged >=10% install64 latency reduction in both windows and no peak increase in any control guard
intervention.preservation: Same source/State/custody laws plus combined unique-prefix allocation-failure tests; all isolated variants retained for attribution

experiments.disposition: Combines prefix preservation with active-frame/node transfer. About 13% install64 improvement, but retains install8 peak increase.

experiments.name: staged

intervention.change: When handler installation has zero actual call operands, allocate its generated-capability argument buffer after capture/pruning. Nonempty operands retain the same pre-transfer staging.
intervention.hypothesis: Earlier allocation of generated-only arguments overlaps pruning scratch and causes the install8 +500-byte peak.
intervention.target: Unchanged latency and peak guards across full matrix
intervention.preservation: Generated references have no input reads; all actual reader operands still gathered before frame phase change. No extra copies or source-specific cases.

experiments.disposition: Discarded no-effect hypothesis: delaying generated arguments does not change the working peak.

intervention.target: Unchanged >=10% install64 gain and no primary/control peak increase
intervention.law: Session constructor or poisoned-step/Resident rollback contains failures before root publication. Same nodes, frame bindings, trace and checkpoint grammar.
intervention.proof: 74 source tests including all allocation failure and allocator reentrancy lanes; full World aggregate and value guards

experiments.disposition: Removes 400 of the 500 excess install8 bytes by allocating the control before its frame; further reservation still needed.

intervention.evidence: Early control allocation removes400B of install8 increase; node-vector growth still overlaps100B of call temporaries.
